text:
incident-bot: PAGED: high-severity alert — EU region tail latency spike observed on economy tier. Latency p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 2.1s, p99 intermittently > 6s. Error rate up small (~0.8%) due to client timeouts. Auto-routing bumped traffic to cheaper nodes which are oversaturated. Paging oncall: @ana is on rotation.

ana: I’m on it — pulling up routing metrics and recent policy changes. Any recent deploys?

mira: No product deploys in EU overnight. We did push a policy tweak to routing weights for economy tier 03:12 UTC (reduce cost by 10%). Could that be related?

jurgen: Confirmed — infra updated routing weights via config orchestration 03:12 UTC. Posting diff:
```
- policy.economy.weight = 0.7
+ policy.economy.weight = 0.45
```
That pushed more economy traffic to lower-cost instances in eu-west-2 which have lower CPU headroom.

leo: Runtime logs show continuous-batching backlog increasing and KV cache misses spiking for those hosts. Those nodes have higher latency for long-context batches. We should consider immediate mitigation: temporarily raise economy weight back and apply per-key rate caps.

ana: Agreed. Short plan: 1) revert routing weight to previous value, 2) apply soft rate cap 12 r/s per API key for economy tier in EU for 10 mins, 3) enable regional fallback to mid-tier for timeouts > 3s, 4) inform support/customer-facing.

ops-bot: Executing runbook: revert routing weights -> running job r-apply-872.

ops-bot: Job r-apply-872 completed: policy.economy.weight set to 0.70 across eu regions.

jurgen: Pushing rate cap now via quota service. Command:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/quotas/apply -d '{"region":"eu","tier":"economy","limit_rps":12,"duration_s":600}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSMAN"
```
Applied.

leo: Monitoring: p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 850ms within two minutes after revert. p99 still spiky at ~1.8s for a subset of keys. KV cache warmup ongoing.

mira: Support — @jamie, can you surface any customer-facing errors or complaints? Need to know if any paying customers hit timeouts.

jamie: Support triage: small fraction of EU paid keys reported client-side timeouts; most recovered. Logged tickets: 2 enterprise customers reported degraded responses between 03:15-03:24 UTC. I’ve escalated both to SEs and sent status note to their contacts.

ana: Good. Next: set a temporary conditional routing override for EU to prefer mid-tier for economy requests that request sequence length > 2048 or have retries > 1. This should reduce long-context pressure on cheap nodes. jurgen/leo can we deploy a policy patch?

jurgen: Preparing patch. Snippet:
```json
{"region":"eu","match":{"tier":"economy","seq_len_gt":2048},"action":{"route_to":"mid","weight":0.9}}
```
Staging apply now (canary 5% traffic).

ops-bot: Canary rollout started: 5% of economy EU traffic diverted to mid-tier nodes. Healthchecks enabled.

leo: Canary metrics look good at 2m: latency p95 for canary group = 420ms, error rate stable. Bumping canary to 25% now.

mira: Product ok with 25% ramp. If stable in 10m, we can make it regional default until full capacity snapback. Customer impact minimal with this approach.

ana: Oncall handoff: I’ll remain until metrics stable for 30m post full ramp. If anything degrades, escalate to SRE lead. Also scheduling a follow-up postmortem.

jamie: Noted — I’ll keep customers informed and update support status page: short outage window 03:12–03:26 UTC, mitigated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress — routing weight reverted, rate caps applied, canary conditional routing active at 25%. Continue monitoring.

leo: Logging mitigation run ids: r-apply-872, quota-3341, canary-apply-559. Saved snapshots for debugging.

ana: Thanks all. Action items: jurgen/leo keep monitoring; mira/jamie coordinate customer comms; oncall (ana) will write blameless incident note and link to telemetry.

mira: Also opening a ticket to add automated detection for routing-weight-induced saturation — alert if p95 increases >50% within 5 mins following weight change.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: metrics rolled back to baseline by 03:40 UTC, p95 stable, p99 < 1.2s for all keys. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

ana: Closing here — moving to #postmortems to collect logs and timeline.
